env.name: OBSIDIAN_API_KEY
env.description: Bearer token for the Obsidian Local REST API plugin (Settings → Community Plugins → Local REST API).

env.name: OBSIDIAN_BASE_URL
env.description: Base URL of the Obsidian Local REST API. Default: http://127.0.0.1:27123 (enable "Non-encrypted (HTTP) Server" in plugin settings). Use https://127.0.0.1:27124 for the always-on HTTPS port (self-signed cert; pair with OBSIDIAN_VERIFY_SSL=false).

env.name: OBSIDIAN_VERIFY_SSL
env.description: Whether to verify the TLS certificate on the Obsidian endpoint. Default false because the plugin uses a self-signed cert.

env.name: OBSIDIAN_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS
env.description: Per-request timeout in milliseconds.

env.name: OBSIDIAN_ENABLE_COMMANDS
env.description: Opt-in flag for the command-palette pair (obsidian_list_commands + obsidian_execute_command). Off by default — Obsidian commands are opaque and can be destructive.

env.name: OBSIDIAN_READ_PATHS
env.description: Optional comma-separated vault-relative folder allowlist for reads. Prefix-based with implicit recursion; case-insensitive; backslashes read as slashes, repeated and trailing slashes and '.' segments dropped, and names normalized to Unicode NFC; an entry naming the vault root ('.') is rejected at startup. Unset = full vault. Write paths are implicitly readable. Example: 'public/,projects/'.

env.name: OBSIDIAN_WRITE_PATHS
env.description: Optional comma-separated vault-relative folder allowlist for writes. Same syntax as OBSIDIAN_READ_PATHS. Unset = full vault, or the read scope when reads are restricted; paths in OBSIDIAN_DENY_PATHS stay denied. Example: 'projects/,scratch/'.

env.name: OBSIDIAN_DENY_PATHS
env.description: Optional comma-separated vault-relative paths withheld from reads and writes. Same syntax as OBSIDIAN_READ_PATHS. Wins over both allowlists; denied paths are left out of listings, search results, and tag counts. Unset = nothing denied. Example: 'private/,journal/therapy/'.

env.name: OBSIDIAN_READ_ONLY
env.description: Global read-only kill switch. When true, every write is denied regardless of OBSIDIAN_WRITE_PATHS, and the command-palette pair is suppressed (commands can mutate). Useful for shared or public-facing deployments.

env.name: OBSIDIAN_DELETE_ELICITATION
env.description: Opt-in delete confirmation. When true, obsidian_delete_note asks the user to confirm each delete through an elicitation round (the client must support elicitation), and HTTP startup requires a stateful session unless OBSIDIAN_READ_ONLY=true disables the tool. Off by default — the delete runs on the first call, bounded by OBSIDIAN_WRITE_PATHS and OBSIDIAN_READ_ONLY.

env.name: OBSIDIAN_OMNISEARCH_URL
env.description: Override URL for the Omnisearch plugin HTTP server. Unset derives from OBSIDIAN_BASE_URL host with port 51361. Required only if the Omnisearch plugin is not on the default port.

env.name: MCP_LOG_LEVEL
env.description: Sets the minimum log level for output (e.g., 'debug', 'info', 'warn').

env.name: MCP_TRANSPORT_TYPE
env.description: Selects the HTTP transport.

env.name: CONFIG
env.description: Path to your configuration file

env.name: MCP_ALLOW_STATIC_FALLBACK
env.description: Set to 'true' to allow HTTP startup when config.json has static credentials. Otherwise the server refuses to start, preventing silent shared-identity fallback for unauthenticated requests.

env.name: MCP_CONTENT_MAX_BYTES
env.description: Byte cap for the content bodies and result blocks tools return (wikitext, rendered HTML, diffs, statement and row listings). An oversized response is truncated with a trailing marker describing what was left out.

env.name: MCP_FILE_DATA_MAX_BYTES
env.description: Hard cap on the base64-encoded size of a get-file-data response. A transport/safety backstop; callers tune actual size with the tool's width parameter. Over-cap responses error rather than truncate.

env.name: MCP_LOG_LEVEL
env.description: Minimum severity for logger output (stderr telemetry and sendLoggingMessage broadcast). Invalid values fail loudly on first log call.

env.name: MCP_MAX_REQUEST_BODY
env.description: Maximum HTTP request body size on the StreamableHTTP transport. Accepts size strings like 1mb or 512kb.

env.name: MCP_METRICS
env.description: Set to 'true' to expose Prometheus metrics at GET /metrics on the HTTP transport. Has no effect on the stdio transport.

env.name: MCP_OAUTH_ALLOWED_REDIRECTS
env.description: Additional allowed redirect URIs for hosted-proxy client registration: comma-separated exact URIs (which must include a host) and https prefix patterns ending in /*. Loopback, claude.ai, and verified first-party clients (ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code) are always allowed; unset means no additional clients.

env.name: MCP_OAUTH_CIMD_ALLOWED_HOSTS
env.description: Comma-separated additional client_id document hosts trusted for CIMD (bare host or host:port). Verified first-party hosts are always trusted.

env.name: MCP_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS_FILE
env.description: Override the default OAuth credentials store path. Default: ~/.config/mediawiki-mcp/credentials.json on Linux/macOS, %APPDATA%\mediawiki-mcp\credentials.json on Windows.

env.name: MCP_OAUTH_NO_BROWSER
env.description: Set to '1' to skip launching a browser during the OAuth dance and log the auth URL to stderr instead. Useful in headless environments and CI.

env.name: MCP_OAUTH_PROXY_STORE_FILE
env.description: Path to the hosted OAuth proxy's encrypted state file, which lets sign-ins survive restarts. Default: proxy-store.enc under the mediawiki-mcp config dir; /app/data/proxy-store.enc in the Docker image.

env.name: MCP_PUBLIC_URL
env.description: Override the request-derived public URL used in the protected-resource discovery doc and WWW-Authenticate header. Set this when running behind a proxy that rewrites the request Host.

env.name: MCP_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_MS
env.description: Maximum milliseconds to wait for in-flight /mcp calls to drain on SIGTERM/SIGINT before exiting. Capped at 600000.

env.name: MCP_TRANSPORT
env.description: Type of MCP server transport

env.name: MCP_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES
env.description: Memory cap on the server-side fetch used by upload-file-from-url and update-file-from-url. Files larger than this are routed to the wiki's own copy-upload instead of being buffered by the server. Guards this server's memory, not the wiki's $wgMaxUploadSize.

env.name: MCP_USER_AGENT
env.description: Replaces the User-Agent header of every outbound request, which defaults to mediawiki-mcp-server/<version> (https://github.com/ProfessionalWiki/MediaWiki-MCP-Server). If you set it, give a name and an email or URL, e.g. 'ExampleBot/1.0 (bot@example.org)'.

env.name: PORT
env.description: Port used for StreamableHTTP transport

env.name: MCP_ENV_PATH
env.description: Path to the .env file that states the destination (the same as the --env-path argument). The file states SAP_URL and SAP_AUTH_TYPE (basic, snc or jwt); a jwt file also states SAP_GRANT_TYPE (authorization_code or none). Without this or --mcp, the server starts in tool-inspection-only mode: nothing is read from the working directory, and SAP_* variables in the process environment alone form no destination.

env.name: AUTH_BROKER_PATH
env.description: Base directory of service-keys/ and sessions/ for a named destination chosen with the --mcp argument (one directory; a list is not split). Default: ~/.config/mcp-abap-adt (Documents\mcp-abap-adt on Windows).

env.name: MCP_BROWSER
env.description: Browser for a JWT login: chrome, edge, firefox, system, headless or none.

env.name: MCP_BROWSER_AUTH_PORT
env.description: Callback port of the JWT browser login, 1-65535.

env.name: MCP_UNSAFE
env.description: Write a named destination's session to disk (sessions/<name>.env) instead of keeping it in memory.

env.name: SAP_CONNECTION_TYPE
env.description: Connection type: http or rfc. SNC needs rfc (and the SAP NW RFC SDK).

env.name: SAP_SYSTEM_TYPE
env.description: System type, required (here or as --system-type; no default, never guessed): the tools offered (e.g. Programs are onprem-only), the connector, and how the system's answers are read. Without it a destination does not start.

env.name: SAP_LANGUAGE
env.description: Logon language (ISO code, e.g. 'en', 'de').

env.name: SAP_MASTER_SYSTEM
env.description: System context for on-prem create/update operations (system id).

env.name: SAP_RESPONSIBLE
env.description: Responsible user for on-prem create/update operations.

servers.title: Vault Cortex

env.name: MCP_AUTH_TOKEN
env.description: Bearer token for MCP client authentication. Must match the Authorization header sent by clients. Generate with: openssl rand -hex 32

env.name: PUBLIC_URL
env.description: Public URL clients use to reach this server. Used as the OAuth issuer URL in discovery metadata. Override when exposing the server outside localhost or on a non-default port.

env.name: EMBEDDING_ENABLED
env.description: Enable or disable the embedding pipeline. When false, no ONNX model is downloaded, no vector tables are created, and search uses FTS5 only.

env.name: RERANK_MODE
env.description: Cross-encoder reranking mode: blended (position-aware score blending after RRF fusion) or none (skip reranking). Only takes effect when EMBEDDING_ENABLED is true.

env.name: WINDOWS_MODE
env.description: Windows bind-mount mode: enables filesystem polling for the file watcher and rename-based moves across the Docker Desktop/WSL2 bridge. Set to true when the vault lives on a Windows drive.

env.name: MEMORY_ENABLED
env.description: Enable or disable the structured memory layer. When false, memory tools are hidden, bootstrap is skipped, and server metadata omits memory references.

env.name: FILE_TOOLS_ENABLED
env.description: Enable or disable file tools (vault_read_file, vault_list_files). When false, file tools are hidden and server metadata omits file tool references.

env.name: READONLY_MODE
env.description: Run the server read-only: every vault-writing tool is hidden, the memory folder is not auto-created, and server metadata omits write references.

env.name: DISABLED_TOOLS
env.description: Hide individual tools by name, comma-separated. Subtractive only — it cannot re-enable a tool another setting hides; an unknown tool name stops the server at startup.

env.name: MEMORY_DIR
env.description: Vault folder for structured memory files (About Me-style notes). Memory tools are hidden when MEMORY_ENABLED is false, but this value still feeds the defaults for PROTECTED_PATHS and ORPHAN_EXCLUDE_FOLDERS.

env.name: DAILY_NOTES_FOLDER
env.description: Vault folder for daily notes. Overrides the folder configured in Obsidian's daily-notes plugin. When unset, read from the vault's .obsidian/daily-notes.json (an empty folder there follows Obsidian's new-note location), falling back to "Daily Notes" when that file is missing or unreadable. Set to / for the vault root.

env.name: DAILY_NOTES_FORMAT
env.description: Filename date format for daily notes (Moment.js tokens). Overrides the format configured in Obsidian's daily-notes plugin. When unset, read from the vault's .obsidian/daily-notes.json, falling back to "YYYY-MM-DD".

env.name: TRUST_PROXY_HOPS
env.description: Number of trusted reverse-proxy hops used to derive the client IP from X-Forwarded-For for OAuth rate limiting and request logs. With 0, injected forwarding headers are ignored.

env.name: TRUST_FORWARDED_HOPS
env.description: How many entries from the end of the RFC 7239 Forwarded header's for= list to count to reach the client IP for OAuth rate limiting and request logs. 0 ignores the header; 1 when the proxy in front writes it (e.g. AWS API Gateway); 2 when a CDN fronts that proxy and is the only way to reach it.

env.name: TZ
env.description: IANA timezone for timestamps and daily note resolution.

env.name: LOG_LEVEL
env.description: Logging verbosity.

env.name: LOG_DIR
env.description: Directory for log files that survive container re-creation. The container's own log is always written but discarded when the container is recreated; date-stamped files under LOG_DIR persist on the data volume. Default: /data/logs (remote image), $STORAGE_ROOT/data/logs (single-volume mode), none (local image). none keeps only the container log.

env.name: LOG_RETENTION_DAYS
env.description: Days to keep log files; cleanup runs at startup and each day. Only applies when LOG_DIR is a path.

env.name: LOG_MAX_DAILY_MB
env.description: Maximum MB per daily log file (1 MB = 1,000,000 bytes). Whole numbers of at least 1, or none to disable the cap. File logging pauses at the cap until midnight in TZ (UTC by default); console logging continues.

env.name: PROTECTED_PATHS
env.description: Comma-separated vault folder names blocked from vault_delete_note and vault_move_note. Default: MEMORY_DIR plus the daily notes folder, read from DAILY_NOTES_FOLDER or .obsidian/daily-notes.json (default Daily Notes; none when that setting is the vault root or empty). When set, overrides the default entirely.

env.name: ORPHAN_EXCLUDE_FOLDERS
env.description: Comma-separated vault folder names excluded from vault_find_orphans. Default: the daily notes folder, "Templates", and MEMORY_DIR. DAILY_NOTES_FOLDER wins; otherwise .obsidian/daily-notes.json is read per query (fallback "Daily Notes"; no daily folder when that setting is the vault root or empty). When set, replaces the defaults entirely. Set to a comma (,) to exclude nothing; an empty value uses the defaults.

env.name: SERVICE_DOCUMENTATION_URL
env.description: Override the OAuth service documentation URL exposed via discovery metadata.

env.name: MAX_FILE_BYTES
env.description: Largest file vault_read_file will read, in bytes. Reading a larger file returns an error instead of content.

env.name: MAX_IMAGE_OUTPUT_BYTES
env.description: Byte budget for images returned by vault_read_file, in binary bytes before base64 encoding. Images exceeding the budget are downscaled/recompressed server-side to fit; raise for clients that accept larger tool responses.

env.name: MAX_PDF_RENDER_PAGES
env.description: Maximum PDF pages to render as images when raw: true is set on vault_read_file. The per-page byte budget is MAX_IMAGE_OUTPUT_BYTES divided evenly across the rendered pages.

env.name: CB_CONNECTION_STRING
env.description: Couchbase connection string. Required for connecting to the cluster.

env.name: CB_USERNAME
env.description: Couchbase database username. Required for basic authentication.

env.name: CB_PASSWORD
env.description: Couchbase database password. Required for basic authentication.

env.name: CB_CA_CERT_PATH
env.description: Couchbase CA certificate path. Required for TLS authentication in non Capella clusters.

env.name: CB_CLIENT_CERT_PATH
env.description: Couchbase client certificate path. Required for mTLS authentication.

env.name: CB_CLIENT_KEY_PATH
env.description: Couchbase client key path. Required for mTLS authentication.

env.name: CB_MCP_READ_ONLY_MODE
env.description: Couchbase read only mode. Set to true to disable write operations: KV document, scope/collection and index write tools are not loaded, and SQL++ queries that modify data are blocked. Set to false to allow them. Default is true.

env.name: CB_MCP_TRANSPORT
env.description: Transport mode for the server (stdio, http or sse). Default is stdio. OAuth is only honored with http.

env.name: CB_MCP_HOST
env.description: Host to run the MCP server on (default: 127.0.0.1). Used only for HTTP and SSE transport modes.

env.name: CB_MCP_PORT
env.description: Port to run the MCP server on (default: 8000). Used only for HTTP and SSE transport modes.

env.name: CB_MCP_WORKERS
env.description: Number of server worker processes (default: 1). Values above 1 use more CPU cores, require the http transport, run in stateless HTTP mode, and cannot be combined with CB_MCP_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED_TOOLS. Each worker writes log files named with the host and process id.

env.name: CB_MCP_STATELESS_HTTP

env.name: CB_MCP_OAUTH_JWT_AUDIENCE
env.description: Expected JWT 'aud' claim value. Required to enable OAuth.

env.description: JWT signing algorithm. One of RS256/384/512, ES256/384/512, PS256/384/512. Default is RS256.

env.name: CB_MCP_OAUTH_MCP_BASE_URL

env.name: CB_MCP_OAUTH_SCOPE_READ_LABEL

env.name: CB_MCP_OAUTH_SCOPE_WRITE_LABEL

env.name: CB_MCP_AUDIT_LOG_ENABLED
env.description: Enable audit logging. Audit output is a separate sink from the CB_MCP_LOG_* operational logs, with a stable schema, its own retention, and events that cannot be filtered out. Default is false.

env.name: CB_MCP_AUDIT_LOG_SINKS
env.description: Comma-separated audit destinations: console, file, or both. 'console' writes to stderr, never stdout, because stdout carries the JSON-RPC protocol under the stdio transport. Default is console.

env.name: CB_MCP_EMBEDDING_MODEL_PROVIDER
env.description: Embedding provider for run_vector_query / run_vector_search: one of capella, openai, cohere, voyage, bedrock. Unset disables both tools' embedding step until configured.

env.name: CB_MCP_AUDIT_LOG_FILE_PATH
env.description: Path to the audit log file, required when 'file' is in CB_MCP_AUDIT_LOG_SINKS. Each server process writes its own file with the host and process id inserted before the extension (audit.log becomes audit.myhost.1234.log), because a stdio deployment runs one process per client. If the path is missing the server still starts, with the file sink dropped and an error recorded.

env.name: CB_MCP_AUDIT_LOG_ROTATION_MAX_SIZE_MB
env.description: Maximum size in MB the live audit file may reach before it rotates. 0 turns size-based rotation off. Default is 10 MB.

env.name: CB_MCP_AUDIT_LOG_ROTATION_INTERVAL
env.description: Age the live audit file may reach before it rotates, as <value><unit> where the unit is 'd' (24 hours) or 'w' (7 days) - for example 1d, 30d, 1w, 8w. 0 turns interval-based rotation off. Size and interval are independent: whichever falls due first rotates the file. Default is 1d.

env.name: CB_MCP_EMBEDDING_MODEL
env.description: Model name/ID for the configured embedding provider.

env.name: CB_MCP_AUDIT_LOG_RETENTION_MAX_BACKUPS

env.name: CB_MCP_AUDIT_LOG_TOOL_ARGS
env.description: Record tool argument values in the audit log. Positive integer, maximum 600; larger values are clamped to 600 with a warning, and any other invalid value is logged as a warning and the default is used. Default is 30.

env.description: Operational Insights read only mode. Set to true to disable write operations: the operational_insights_create_index and operational_insights_cancel_async_query tools are not loaded, and queries that modify data are blocked. Set to false to allow them. Default is true.

env.name: CB_MCP_PORT

env.name: CB_MCP_STATELESS_HTTP

env.name: CB_MCP_DISABLED_TOOLS

env.name: OPCUA_SERVER_URL
env.description: URL of the OPC UA server to connect to, including any path the server expects. Read once at startup: one process serves one endpoint. Verify who answers with an exact server certificate pin or a configured CA trust store.

env.name: OPCUA_PYTHON_BACKEND
env.description: Select the Python client implementation. The maintained asyncua client is the default; legacy provides the one-release rollback path for uncovered vendor incompatibilities. This setting affects the Python server only.

env.name: OPCUA_SECURITY_POLICY
env.description: Encryption suite to negotiate for the secure channel. Anything other than None needs a client certificate and key. The two AES suites are Node-only: the Python runtime refuses them at startup rather than downgrading. None is unencrypted and unauthenticated, and keeps control tools blocked unless insecure control is explicitly allowed. An unknown policy stops the server at startup.

env.name: OPCUA_SECURITY_MODE
env.description: Message security mode for the secure channel. Sign authenticates messages without encrypting them. A policy with mode None, or a mode without a policy, stops the server at startup; leaving it blank never downgrades a policy to signing only. Leave blank for SignAndEncrypt once a security policy is set, otherwise None.

env.name: OPCUA_CLIENT_CERT
env.description: Path to the certificate (PEM or DER) this client presents as its application identity. Required by any security policy other than None. A path that does not exist stops the server at startup.

env.name: OPCUA_CLIENT_KEY
env.description: Path to the private key matching the client certificate. A path, never key material. Whoever can read the file can impersonate this client: keep it readable only by the account running the server. A path that does not exist stops the server at startup.

env.name: OPCUA_APPLICATION_URI
env.description: Application URI announced to the server. Set it only for a certificate that carries no URI of its own. A configured URI that conflicts with the certificate is refused before connecting. Leave blank for the subjectAltName URI of the client certificate.

env.name: OPCUA_SERVER_CERT
env.description: Path to the OPC UA server's own certificate (PEM or DER), pinned: a server presenting any other certificate cannot complete the handshake. Control tools (writes, method calls, alarm actions) require it, or OPCUA_SERVER_TRUST_STORE instead. Requires a security policy other than None. Unset, encryption protects against eavesdropping but not against an impostor endpoint, so control tools are refused unless OPCUA_SERVER_TRUST_STORE validates the server or OPCUA_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_SERVER_CONTROL is set. Set without a security policy, it stops the server at startup rather than pinning nothing; a pinned certificate that has expired or is not yet valid refuses to connect.

env.name: OPCUA_SERVER_TRUST_STORE
env.description: Directory with trusted/certs root CAs, issuers/certs intermediate CAs, and trusted/crl plus issuers/crl signed current revocation lists. Authenticate the OPC UA peer by its validated chain and expected server URI. Requires secured channel and OPCUA_SERVER_APPLICATION_URI; Python requires the maintained asyncua backend. Missing, stale, forged or revoked trust material refuses connection. Cannot be combined with an exact server certificate pin.

env.name: OPCUA_SERVER_APPLICATION_URI
env.description: ApplicationUri of the intended OPC UA server. Must match the peer certificate URI SAN and advertised application identity. Required with OPCUA_SERVER_TRUST_STORE.

env.name: OPCUA_USERNAME
env.description: OPC UA username. The session is anonymous when unset. Cannot be combined with a user certificate. Requires a password; either one alone stops the server at startup.

env.name: OPCUA_PASSWORD
env.description: Password for the username. Without a security policy it crosses the network in clear text. Supply it through the client's secret storage, never on a command line.

env.name: OPCUA_USER_CERT
env.description: Path to the certificate identifying the user, for X.509 user authentication: a different key pair from the client certificate, which secures the channel. Requires the user key and a security policy other than None; cannot be combined with a username. Any of those combinations broken stops the server at startup.

env.name: OPCUA_USER_KEY
env.description: Path to the private key for the user certificate. It signs the server's challenge and is never sent. Whoever can read the file can log in as this user: keep it readable only by the account running the server.

env.name: OPCUA_PROFILE
env.description: Which tools are offered. observe reads, browses, reads history and monitors; operator adds explicitly allowlisted writes, method calls and alarm actions; full exposes every tool and is meant only for a tightly scoped OPC UA account. Unset fails closed to observe; an unknown profile stops the server at startup.

env.name: OPCUA_POLICY_FILE
env.description: Path to a version-1 JSON policy file, the only place per-node value bounds, writable_subtrees, preconditions, the alarm scope and deny_read can be set. Every policy variable that is set overrides what the file says. An unreadable or invalid file stops the server at startup.

env.name: OPCUA_ALLOWED_TOOLS
env.description: Comma-separated tool allowlist. It can only narrow the selected profile, never widen it. An unknown tool name stops the server at startup.

env.name: OPCUA_ALLOWED_WRITE_NODES
env.description: Comma-separated exact node IDs the operator profile may write, as ns=2;i=5 or, stable across a server restart, nsu=<namespace-uri>;i=5 or a browse path from the Root folder such as /Objects/Line1/Setpoint. Setting it replaces the policy file's list, bounds included. Empty fails closed: operator can write nothing. A batch write with any target outside the list is refused before it reaches OPC UA.

env.name: OPCUA_ALLOWED_METHODS
env.description: Comma-separated object_node_id|method_node_id pairs the operator profile may call. Either half may be a browse path from the Root folder. Empty fails closed: operator can call nothing. An entry without | stops the server at startup.

env.name: OPCUA_ALLOW_ACKNOWLEDGE_ALARMS
env.description: Let the operator profile act on alarms: acknowledge_alarm and every act_on_alarm action.

env.name: OPCUA_ALLOW_INSECURE_CONTROL
env.description: Permit control tools on an OPC UA channel with no security policy (None). Does not cover a secured channel to an unverified server; that is OPCUA_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_SERVER_CONTROL. Fail-open override: writes, method calls and alarm actions then travel unauthenticated and unencrypted. Reported as control=INSECURE-OVERRIDE in the startup line, get_server_status and every audit record. Never enable it against production equipment.

env.name: OPCUA_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_SERVER_CONTROL
env.description: Permit control tools on a secured OPC UA channel whose server is not authenticated: neither pinned with OPCUA_SERVER_CERT nor validated by OPCUA_SERVER_TRUST_STORE. Does not cover a channel with no security policy; that is OPCUA_ALLOW_INSECURE_CONTROL. Fail-open override: writes, method calls and alarm actions are then encrypted to whichever server answered the endpoint, which may be an impostor. Reported as control=UNVERIFIED-OVERRIDE in the startup line, get_server_status and every audit record. Never enable it against production equipment.

env.name: OPCUA_ALLOW_OUT_OF_RANGE_WRITES
env.description: Allow a write outside the EURange the OPC UA server itself published for the node. A published InstrumentRange still applies. Fail-open override: it discards the only value bound a deployment with no policy file has.

env.name: OPCUA_AUDIT_FILE
env.description: Path to an append-only file for the control audit trail, one JSON object per line, written beside stderr. Created owner-only (0600) if it does not exist; reopened when rotated away. A file that cannot be opened, or that is a symlink, not a regular file, another account's, or group/world-writable, stops the server rather than falling back to stderr alone. While set, a control call whose record cannot be written is refused (fail closed); reads continue.

env.name: OPCUA_AUDIT_FSYNC
env.description: When an audit-file record counts as written. always fsyncs each record before the control call proceeds, so it survives a power loss; none leaves it to the operating system, so it survives only a crash of this process. none can lose the records of control calls that already reached the plant if the machine loses power.

env.name: OPCUA_AUDIT_CHAIN
env.description: Adds seq, prev_hash and hash to every audit record so edits, deletions and reordering can be detected with --verify-audit. sha256 catches accidental or naive edits; hmac-sha256 also resists anyone without the key. Requires the audit file. Set without an audit file, or hmac-sha256 without a key file, stops the server. No chain detects a truncated tail.

env.name: OPCUA_AUDIT_CHAIN_KEY_FILE
env.description: Path to the HMAC key for the hmac-sha256 audit chain: at least 32 bytes, for example from openssl rand -hex 32. Surrounding whitespace is ignored. Whoever can read the key can forge the chain: a key readable or writable by group or others stops the server. Refused unless the chain is hmac-sha256.

env.name: OPCUA_OPERATOR_ID
env.description: Label stamped on every audit record as operator_label, so a shipped log says which deployment a control call came from. Configured, never verified: it is not an identity, and mcp_principal stays null.

env.name: OPCUA_RECONNECT_INITIAL_DELAY_MS
env.description: Wait before the first attempt to repair a dropped or refused connection, in milliseconds. It doubles with each further attempt.

env.name: OPCUA_RECONNECT_MAX_DELAY_MS
env.description: Ceiling for the doubling retry delay, in milliseconds.

env.name: OPCUA_RECONNECT_MAX_RETRY
env.description: Retries after the first attempt, per connection round, before a tool call gives up: a whole number from -1 to 1000. 0 never retries; -1 never stops trying, in bounded rounds of four retries so no single call waits forever.

env.name: OPCUA_SESSION_TIMEOUT_MS
env.description: Session lifetime asked of the OPC UA server, in milliseconds. It also sets the keep-alive period, so it decides how quickly an idle connection notices the server has gone.
